title: Stale mechanism comment in adaptive_sf_step3_uses_spec_density_8 (claims density threshold 8, actual DENSITY_HIGH=10)
description: Found during 5m15 edge-cases review (kimi-k3). rust/lichen-core/src/rf_health.rs:717-733 test adaptive_sf_step3_uses_spec_density_8 asserts sf=11 correctly, but its comment describes the wrong mechanism: it claims 'density 9 > 8: step 3 engages (+2) per spec 2a.8 (was > 10), then floor (c) lifts the result to 11'. In this tree DENSITY_HIGH=10 (rf_health.rs:16), so step 3 and floor (c) do not fire at density 9; the assertion actually passes via floor (b) (SNR EMA -2 < SNR_POOR=0 -> max(11)). Assertions are correct; only the described mechanism is wrong. Fix the comment to describe floor (b), and reconsider the test name if the density-8 threshold is no longer what it exercises.
close_reason: Stale comment and misleading test name corrected: adaptive_sf_step3_uses_spec_density_8 -> adaptive_sf_floor_b_engages_below_density_high. Verified against spec 02a (DENSITY_HIGH=10, constants table :162; 'When Density > DENSITY_HIGH (10)' :560) — the code is spec-conformant; only the comment claimed a density-8 threshold. New comments describe the true mechanisms: floor (b) via SNR EMA -2 < SNR_POOR=0 at density 9 <= 10; benign pass-through at density 8/SNR 10. Assertions unchanged. 48/48 rf_health tests pass. 3x codereview delegated to kimi-k3: correctness PASS (comment claims verified against constants), security PASS (stale comment was a documentation hazard for density-signaling analysis), edge-cases PASS (DENSITY_HIGH=10/11 boundaries independently pinned by adaptive_sf_density_threshold_is_ten and adaptive_sf_floors_apply_in_order — no coverage gap).
